rv.q: This delightfully weird and just plain delightful show will provide the kind of thrills we look for in all musical comedies.
Penned by the Canadian team of Brooke Maxwell and Jacob Richmond, "Ride the Cyclone" is a work at once macabre and sweet, melancholy and affirmative, merciless and deeply compassionate.
But at 100 minutes, this gaudily hand-painted car trundles along after the thrill has faded.
As a result it’s a little bit of all of the above, except for the last.
The impulse toward the easy, cheesy laugh means that unlike other teen-angst musicals, the emotional stakes remain flat.

The potential for serious exploration of the horror show that is teenage society is certainly there, but Ride the Cyclone plays more like a talent show where each character's big number is checked off before some kind of philosophy is introduced to fabricate an ending.
Some people will love its unchallenging and tuneful humor, while others will bristle at its mindless philosophizing.
'Ride the Cyclone' looks and sounds much better than it is, thanks to Rachel Rockwell's direction and choreography and a top-flight cast of fresh faces.

cn.t: This quirky musical about dead teens divides critics: some find it delightfully weird with a superlative cast, while others criticize flat emotions, derivative material, and a forced concept that struggles to balance its dark premise with comedy.
